newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch confirms downward adjustment to NZ surplus.
newsitem.headline: Birch confirms downward adjustment to NZ surplus.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch on Tuesday confirmed next week's pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update would show a downward adjustment to the size of the budget surplus in 1996/97.
* a judgement against the government in a court case over the 1987 sale of New Zealand Steel to Equiticorp, where the government had to pay NZ$189 million plus $133 million in costs
* an increase in the unfunded liability of the Government Superannuation Fund
* short-term costs of buying back long-term foreign current debt.
The operating surplus would still be the strongest New Zealand had seen in decades.
"The surplus will continue to reach unprecedented highs over the next four years," he said.
Net public debt as a percentage of GDP would be paid back to levels New Zealand had last seen at the end of the 1970s when it was under 20 percent, he said.
Treasury's pre-election update will be issued on September 12, a month before New Zealanders go to the polls.
